questions.solution:
For each node, a node with no child contributes 1; otherwise its count comes from its children. Then the count for the right siblings is added.

So only nodes without children (leaves) are counted.

Answer: number of leaf nodes in the tree

questions.text:
Consider a hash table with 100 slots. Collisions are resolved using chaining. Assuming
simple uniform hashing, what is the probability that the first 3 slots are unfilled after the first 3 insertions?
questions.solution:
With chaining, each key independently goes to any of the 100 slots. The chance it avoids the first 3 slots is 97/100.

For 3 insertions: [latex]\frac{97\times97\times97}{100^3}[/latex]

Answer: (97 [latex]\times[/latex] 97 [latex]\times[/latex] 97) / [latex]100^3[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Suppose we have a balanced binary search tree T holding n numbers. We are given two numbers L and H and wish to sum up all the numbers in T that lie between L and H. Suppose there are m such numbers in T. If the tightest upper bound on the time to compute the sum is [latex]O(n^{a}log^{b}n+m^{c}log^{d}n)[/latex], the value of a + 10b + 100c + 1000d is _______.
questions.solution:
Find L in the balanced BST in [latex]O(\log n)[/latex], then walk in-order through the m values up to H in O(m).

Time = [latex]O(\log n+m)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a = 0, b = 1, c = 1, d = 0

a + 10b + 100c + 1000d = 0 + 10 + 100 + 0 = 110

Answer: 110

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Consider the following rooted tree with the vertex labelled P as the root

The order in which the nodes are visited during an in-order traversal of the tree is
questions.solution:
In-order for a general tree: in-order of the first child, then the node, then in-order of the remaining children.

- P: (Q-subtree) P (R-subtree)
- Q-subtree: S Q
- R-subtree: T R (U-subtree) V, with U-subtree = W U

Order: S Q P T R W U V

Answer: SQPTRWUV

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Suppose a stack implementation supports an instruction REVERSE, which reverses the order
of elements on the stack, in addition to the PUSH and POP instructions. Which one of the
following statements is TRUE with respect to this modified stack?
questions.solution:
Keep the front of the queue at the top of the stack.

- ENQUEUE(x): REVERSE, PUSH x, REVERSE (3 instructions)
- DEQUEUE: POP (1 instruction)

Answer: ENQUEUE takes three instructions and DEQUEUE takes one

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: A queue cannot be implemented using this stack.

A queue can be implemented where ENQUEUE takes a single instruction and
DEQUEUE takes a sequence of two instructions.

A queue can be implemented where ENQUEUE takes a sequence of three instructions
and DEQUEUE takes a single instruction

A queue can be implemented where both ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE take a single
instruction each.
